calories.title: Why This Deficit/Surplus?
calories.explanation: Your calorie goal is calculated based on your TDEE (total daily energy expenditure) plus your objective. Deficit for fat loss, surplus for muscle gain.
calories.scientific: A calorie deficit creates the optimal hormonal environment for fat loss while preserving muscle mass (Helms et al., 2014).

protein.title: Why 1.6-2.2g/kg of Protein?
protein.explanation: Protein is the most important macronutrient for muscle protein synthesis. Each gram provides essential amino acids to repair and build muscle.
protein.scientific: High-quality protein intake every 3-4 hours maximizes muscle protein synthesis (Morton et al., 2018).

carbs.title: Why Carbohydrates?
carbs.explanation: Carbohydrates are the primary fuel for intense workouts. They provide glucose to maintain energy and preserve muscle glycogen.
carbs.scientific: Carbohydrates maintain muscle glycogen levels, crucial for performance and recovery (Burke et al., 2011).

fats.title: Why Healthy Fats?
fats.explanation: Fats are essential for hormone production, fat-soluble vitamin absorption, and brain health. Balance is key to optimizing testosterone and recovery.
examples: Avoid excess that complicates fat loss
fats.scientific: Healthy fats are precursors to anabolic hormones like testosterone (Volek et al., 2015).

biomechanics_basics.title: How Does Muscle Grow?
biomechanics_basics.description: Understand the science behind muscle growth
biomechanics_basics.introduction: Muscle growth, or hypertrophy, occurs when you subject your muscles to stress that exceeds their current capacity. Here we explain how this fascinating process works.

sections.title: The Hypertrophy Process
sections.content: When you lift weights, you create micro-tears in the muscle fibers. Your body responds by repairing these tears, making the muscles larger and stronger. This process requires: 1) Progressive training, 2) Proper nutrition, 3) Sufficient rest.

sections.title: Influencing Factors
sections.content: Genetics play an important role, but consistent training can maximize your potential. Hypertrophy occurs mainly in type II fibers, which are responsible for strength and muscle size.

sections.title: Common Myths
sections.content: You don't need to train every day. Muscles need 48-72 hours to fully recover. Growth occurs during rest, not during training.

keyTakeaways: Muscles grow during rest, not training
Genetics influence, but consistent training maximizes potential

quiz.question: When does muscle growth actually occur?
quiz.explanation: Muscle growth occurs during recovery and rest phases, when the body repairs the micro-tears caused by training.

quiz.question: What type of muscle fibers are responsible for growth?
quiz.explanation: Type II fibers respond best to strength training and are primarily responsible for muscle growth.

nutrition_101.title: Nutrition 101: Macros and Micros
nutrition_101.description: Master the fundamentals of nutrition for fitness
nutrition_101.introduction: Nutrition is 80% of fitness success. Understanding macros (proteins, carbs, fats) and micros (vitamins, minerals) is crucial to optimizing your results.

sections.title: The 3 Macronutrients
sections.content: Proteins: Muscle building blocks (1.6-2.2g/kg). Carbohydrates: Primary energy source (2-3g/kg for active people). Fats: Hormones and vitamin absorption (0.8-1g/kg).

sections.title: Essential Micronutrients
sections.content: Vitamins and minerals that support recovery, immunity, and performance. Especially important: Vitamin D, Zinc, Magnesium, Iron, and B complex.

sections.title: Nutritional Timing
sections.content: Pre-workout: Carbs for energy. Post-workout: Protein + carbs for recovery. Distributing meals every 3-4 hours maintains stable levels.

keyTakeaways: Protein is essential for muscle growth
Carbohydrates are your primary energy source

quiz.question: What is the general protein recommendation per kg of body weight?
quiz.explanation: For active people looking to gain muscle, 1.6-2.2g of protein per kg of body weight is recommended.

quiz.question: Which macronutrient is most important immediately after training?
quiz.explanation: Protein is crucial post-workout to initiate the recovery process and muscle protein synthesis.

recovery_importance.title: The Science of Rest
recovery_importance.description: Why rest is as important as training
recovery_importance.introduction: Rest is not lost time - it's when the transformation happens. Proper recovery is essential for sustainable progress.

sections.title: Sleep and Recovery
sections.content: During deep sleep, growth hormone is released, crucial for muscle repair. 7-9 hours of quality sleep is minimal for athletes.

sections.title: Active Rest
sections.content: Total rest days or light activities like walking allow recovery without losing cardiovascular condition. Specific muscle rest is key.

sections.title: Signs of Overtraining
sections.content: Chronic fatigue, persistent pain, loss of strength, irritability. If you experience these symptoms, you need more rest.

keyTakeaways: Sleep is when real muscle growth occurs
Rest days are part of the training program
Listening to your body prevents injuries and overtraining

quiz.question: How many hours of sleep are minimally recommended for active people?
quiz.explanation: Active people need 7-9 hours of quality sleep for optimal recovery and growth hormone release.

fat_loss_vs_muscle.title: Fat Loss vs Muscle Gain
fat_loss_vs_muscle.description: Understand the differences and how to balance both goals
fat_loss_vs_muscle.introduction: Losing fat while gaining muscle is possible but requires strategy. Understanding the difference between these processes will help you optimize your results.

sections.title: Fat Loss
sections.content: Requires a calorie deficit (burning more calories than you consume). Cardiovascular exercise accelerates this, but the deficit is most important.

sections.title: Muscle Gain
sections.content: Requires a calorie surplus and progressive strength training. Protein is crucial to provide the necessary amino acids.

sections.title: Body Recomposition
sections.content: Beginners can lose fat and gain muscle simultaneously. Advanced trainees need separate phases. Strength training preserves muscle mass during a deficit.

keyTakeaways: Beginners can recompose, advanced need separate phases

quiz.question: What is most important for losing fat?
quiz.explanation: Although cardio helps, a calorie deficit (consuming fewer calories than you burn) is the most important factor for losing fat.

supplementation_guide.title: Supplementation: What Works, What Doesn't
supplementation_guide.introduction: Supplements can help, but they don't replace good nutrition and training. Here we tell you which ones are worth it and which ones are marketing.

sections.title: Proven Supplements
sections.content: Protein powder: Convenient for reaching protein goals. Creatine: Increases strength and muscle mass. Vitamin D: Essential if you don't have sun exposure. Omega-3: Anti-inflammatory.

sections.title: Marketing vs Science
sections.content: Fat burners: Mostly caffeine. Pre-workouts: Temporary stimulants. BCAAs: Unnecessary if you eat enough protein. Many supplements are expensive placebos.

sections.title: When to Use Supplements
sections.content: When you can't get nutrients from food. To optimize performance when you already have solid bases. Not as shortcuts for bad habits.

keyTakeaways: Food is the base, supplements are extras
Creatine and protein are the most proven

quiz.question: What is the most studied and effective supplement?
quiz.explanation: Creatine is one of the most studied supplements and has consistently shown to increase strength and muscle mass.
